searches.note: Eighteen searches of a share of twenty eight, ten left unspent, none of them the author's. Shared: Olaszrizling's rank in Hungary and the Mátra's main grapes (restricted to bor.hu and winesofhungary.hu, read as primary), the Debrői Hárslevelű designation (the national wine authority's product specification) and the Pata Wine Community's festival. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail rested on the author's reading alone and no search of this check found it, it was cut (the Wine Palace's capacity, the Hajdú tenure, Farkasmály, the Kis-Benedek trap, Gyöngyözőbor's blend).
Prices met on the houses' product pages and in search summaries were not used.
sharedSources: Magyar Bor: Hungary's favourite grape varieties, https://bor.hu/en/magazine/hungarys-favourite-grape-varieties/ (search): Olaszrizling among the most widely planted, Bianca the most planted white.

patch.wine.name: Peres Cuvée
patch.wine.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc, as the house gives the blend, in no fixed share.
patch.wine.sites: The Peres vineyard at Gyöngyöspata, on the Mátra's southern foothills near the family's home village of Gyöngyöstarján; the house calls the wine a selection from that single site.
patch.wine.making: Aged in barrique, the small oak barrel, as the house describes its flagship; the house publishes no months of ageing and no detail of its fermentation, so the record gives none.
patch.wine.glass: Blackcurrant with vanilla and dark chocolate from the barrels, as the house's notes for its barrique aged Cabernets describe them; dry and full, a big red wine, as the house calls it.
patch.wine.ageing: Open it a few years after the vintage, once the oak has settled into the fruit; the house gives no drinking window of its own.
patch.wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour; a Bordeaux glass.

wine.label.means: The Peres vineyard at Gyöngyöspata, from which the house selects the wine.

patch.table: Peres Cuvée is the wine Szőke Mátyás calls its flagship: Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc from the Peres vineyard at Gyöngyöspata, aged in barrique. Expect blackcurrant, vanilla and dark chocolate; decant a young bottle and pour it at 16 to 18 degrees.
patch.story: The family has made wine at Gyöngyöstarján since the 1970s, as the house tells it: its head, an engineer by training, took up winemaking in earnest then, and his son, trained as a winemaker, later joined him in the cellar, so the house carries both their names, family name first in the Hungarian order. The family vineyards lie around the village on the Mátra's southern foothills, among them Hajnal-hegy and Száraz-völgy, and at Gyöngyöspata to the west, where the Peres vineyard gives the house its red flagship. In 2017 the Hungarian Wine Academy named the founder Winemaker of the Year, chosen from the nominations of hundreds of sommeliers, restaurateurs and other professionals, and he was the first from the Mátra in the award's history; his reds had more than once been judged the district's leading red at its own competition. The house is known for a broad range, from Irsai Olivér, a Hungarian crossing first bred in 1930, and a semi sweet Muscat Ottonel to Chardonnay and Merlot, but it names Peres Cuvée, a Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc aged in barrique and selected from one site, as its flagship. For a sommelier, the wine answers a guest who thinks of the Mátra as white wine country: a Bordeaux pair of grapes grown on volcanic foothills, from a cellar whose founder put the district on the national map.

tension: The region record's or plan's description of Olaszrizling as the Mátra's lead white grape, if it says so (the plan's why for Dubicz calls it the district's lead white grape), stands against Magyar Bor, which gives Irsai Olivér as the grape the Mátra grows most; reported, never edited.
